title: Spot It! Free! — How to Play
description: A free picture-only detective flashlight game for classroom vocabulary practice. Use the 8-food starter set or upload your own pictures, arrange and resize clues, and save activities using JSON.
steps: Open Spot It! Free! and select Go to Settings. No Premium account is required.
Choose the editable 8-food preset to play immediately, or select Create New Set to build your own activity.
To add a clue, enter its name and upload or paste a picture. The Free game uses picture clues only; words and letters cannot be used as standalone hidden clues. Names appear on discovery flashcards.
Review the clue list. Use Edit to change a clue name or replace its picture, or Delete to remove it.
Choose the single built-in background or upload your own background picture. Adjust the spotlight size and music or sound-effects controls as needed.
Select Edit Object Positions. Drag each picture to its hiding place. Drag the resize handle to make it larger or smaller. Rotation is not available in Free.
Select Save Positions & Settings to return to the workshop, then choose Start Game.
After the 3, 2, 1, GO! countdown, move the flashlight around the dark scene with your mouse, finger, or smart-board touch.
A picture can be collected only when the flashlight is shining on it. Move the spotlight first, then tap the illuminated picture. Touching a hidden picture outside the beam should not collect it.
Each correctly found picture triggers a discovery flashcard showing the image and its name. Ask students to say the vocabulary word aloud.
Find every picture to complete the mission. Review the collected picture flashcards, score, and elapsed time.
Select Restart to replay or End Game to return to the title screen. Use Full Screen when your browser supports it.
To save a customized activity, select Export JSON. Later, use Import JSON to reopen the activity, check its pictures and positions, and start again.

jsonHelp: Open Go to Settings and prepare your picture clues, background, and positions.
Select Save Changes, then Export JSON to download the activity file.
Keep the .json file on your computer or drive so you can reuse it in another class.
To restore it, choose Import JSON in Settings and select the file.
Check that all images display correctly. Uploaded pictures may be embedded in JSON, while built-in preset photos require the matching photos/ files on the website.
The Free game is picture-only. If you import a Premium activity, review it before playing; Premium-only settings such as team mode and rotation are not available.

sections.title: Classroom activity ideas
steps: Food vocabulary: Use the eight food pictures. After each discovery, ask: What is it? Students answer: It is pizza.
Custom vocabulary: Upload pictures of animals, classroom objects, transportation, or places in the community.
Speaking practice: Let a student move the flashlight while classmates describe the discovered picture in a complete sentence.

sections.title: Free version limits
steps: Solo play only; Detective A versus Detective B team mode is reserved for Premium.
Picture clues only; hidden standalone words and letters are not available.
You may move and resize clues, but cannot rotate them.
One built-in background is included; you may upload your own.
JSON import and export are available.

tips: For the starter foods, keep the matching PNG files in the photos/ folder.
The built-in background is expected at backgrounds/background.png. Upload that file to the backgrounds folder; the HTML alone does not contain it.
Use landscape orientation on phones for a wider play area. On iPhones, Safari generally cannot force landscape orientation or true fullscreen; rotate the device manually.
Keep clues away from the edges and test spotlight movement and tapping on your classroom smart board before the lesson.
A clue should be tapped only after it is illuminated by the flashlight.
